title: Eid Milk
opening: Eid is in a week. The notebook has a milk page, and it is much more badly stained.

intro.p: The children in the lane have been asking for something sweeter than Dadu's dark bar.

talk: Laila beta! The dark bar was a hit, but the children want something sweeter for Eid.
Sweeter? Dadu made a milk bar too. I think.
Sweet, but still chocolatey, mind you. Not just sugar with a brown colour.
Then I need to find out how much cacao, how much sugar and how much milk.
I have written it all on an order slip. Do not lose it, beta.
Fine. The milk page is stained again. I will start with a taste test.

lines.text: Taste the two trial bars. Keep the one that is sweet, but still tastes of [[blur:chocolate]].
Mix the cacao, the sugar and the milk powder. [[torn:…a quarter of the bar is milk, and the sugar is whatever is left.]]
Conche it. [[q:Milk: half the night, and round up. Milk forgives nothing.]]
Temper it cooler than the dark bar. Melt to the red tape. Cool to the blue. Bring it back up to the milk tag.
Pour into the moulds. Tap the tray to knock the air out.

workshop.sceneAlt: Dadu's workshop a week before Eid. Tap the glowing objects to remember.
workshop.hintLine: Tap the glowing spots. Dadu left clues all over the workshop.

clues.title: Rafiq Bhai's Eid order
clues.text: Sweet but still chocolatey, please. For the children. Eid is in a week.

artText.alt: An order slip from Rafiq Bhai: sweet but still chocolatey, please, for the children, Eid is in a week

clues.title: Dadu's milk note
clues.text: "Milk: half the night, and round up. Milk forgives nothing." He wrote it in pencil on the back of a flour sack.

artText.alt: Dadu's pencil note on a flour sack: Milk, half the night, and round up. Milk forgives nothing.

clues.title: The milk powder tin
clues.text: The label is in Dadu's handwriting: "Milk powder. A quarter of every milk bar."

artText.alt: A tin of milk powder with a handwritten label: A quarter of every milk bar

clues.title: The Eid lantern
clues.text: Dadu hung this up every year, a week before Eid. The workshop always smelled of warm milk after that.

artText.alt: An Eid lantern hanging in the workshop

clues.title: The tea tin
clues.text: Half full. He drank his tea before dawn, right after the first azaan.

clues.title: Dadu's thermometer
clues.text: Dadu stopped reading the numbers years ago. He put coloured tape where each one lived. The little tag is his reminder for the milk bars, which are a different recipe.

artText.alt: Dadu's thermometer with a red tape marked {red} at 45 degrees, a blue tape marked {blue} at 27 degrees, a green tape marked {green} at 31 degrees, and a tag reading milk: 29

steps.title: Taste test
steps.prompt: Taste both trial bars. Which one fits the order slip?
steps.say: Two trial bars. The order slip says what the children want.

options.label: Bar A
options.sense: Very sweet and creamy. You taste milk and sugar first, and the chocolate fades fast.
options.no: Bar A is all milk and sugar. The slip says still chocolatey. Try the other one.

options.label: Bar B
options.sense: Sweet and creamy, with a clear cocoa taste that stays on your tongue.

params.idleSense: Tap a bar to taste it.

feedback.correct: Bar B. Sweet, but the chocolate is still in charge.

hints: Read the order slip in the Workshop. What do the children want?
Bar B is sweet but still tastes of chocolate. That is the one on the slip.

steps.title: Line 2: the mix
steps.prompt: One batch is 1 kg. Set how much is cacao, how much is milk powder and how much is sugar.
steps.say: The cacao comes from the bar I kept. The milk tin should say how much milk. Sugar is the rest.

sliders.label: Cacao
sliders.high: Hmm, this is nearly a dark bar again. The children will say it is bitter.
sliders.low: This is mostly sugar and milk. It will taste thin, like Bar A.

sliders.label: Milk powder
sliders.high: Too much milk. It will be soft and pale, and the cocoa taste will vanish.
sliders.low: Not enough milk. It will not taste creamy enough to be a milk bar.

params.remainderHigh: There is too much sugar. It will taste sweeter than Dadu's bar.
params.remainderLow: There is not enough sugar. It will taste less sweet than the children want.

feedback.correct: Forty, thirty-five, twenty-five. Creamy and sweet, and still properly chocolate.

hints: You kept a bar at the taste test, and the milk tin in the Workshop has a label.
Cacao 40, milk powder 25, and the sugar is what is left: 35.

steps.title: Line 3: conche
steps.prompt: Set how many hours the conche should turn.
steps.say: Dadu wrote a rule for milk. It uses the same night as the dark bar.

feedback.correct: Six hours. Half of eleven is five and a half, and Dadu said round up.
feedback.near: Close, but Dadu was exact. Half the dark bar's night, then round up.
feedback.low: It is still gritty. Even milk needs more than that.
feedback.high: Milk forgives nothing. It has gone dull and scorched at that length.

hints: Dadu's milk note says how long, compared with the dark bar. Check the Memory shelf for the dark bar's hours.
The dark bar ran 11 hours. Half is 5 and a half, and round up makes 6.

steps.title: Line 4: temper
steps.prompt: Set the three temperatures. Milk is worked cooler than dark.
steps.say: Red, blue, and the tag on Dadu's thermometer. The tag is for milk bars.

rows.label: Melt
rows.low: Too cool to melt every crystal. The bar would come out streaky.

rows.label: Cool
rows.low: Too cold. It thickens before it can set properly.
rows.high: Still too warm. The good crystals cannot form yet.

rows.label: Rewarm
rows.low: Too cool. It will set thick and dull.
rows.high: Too warm for milk. It undoes the crystals and can scorch.

feedback.correct: Forty-five, twenty-seven, twenty-nine. Glossy, and nothing scorched.

hints: Look at Dadu's thermometer in the Workshop. It has red and blue tape, and a little tag for milk bars.
Red is 45, blue is 27, and the milk tag says 29.

steps.title: Last line: mould
steps.prompt: The chocolate is poured. Tap the tray six times to knock the air out.
steps.say: Pour, then knock the air out.

feedback.correct: The air is out. Now it just has to set.

talk: "Sweet, and still chocolate. The children will not leave you alone."
Can we have it every Eid?
Every Eid. I think Dadu would like that.
recipe: Conche 6 hours, half the night rounded up
Mould and tap out the air
reveal.realFact: In real life, milk scorches easily, so milk chocolate is worked cooler. Many makers conche milk chocolate for as long as dark, just at a lower temperature. Half the time was Dadu's own house rule.

artText.alt: A wrapped bar of Dadu's Eid milk chocolate
